prompt: Summarize this scientific methods section into a single paragraph a journalist could use, explicitly flagging any part of the methodology that limits how strongly the results can be generalized: 'Participants (n=45, convenience sample from a single university) completed a 6-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions via a mobile app. Self-reported stress levels were measured using the PSS-10 scale at baseline and post-intervention. response_text: In a new study exploring the effects of mindfulness on stress, researchers recruited 45 participants—all students from a single university—who took part in a six-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions delivered via a mobile app. Stress levels were tracked using the widely used **Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10)** before and after the program. While the findings suggest potential benefits, the study’s **lack of a control group** and reliance on a **small, convenience sample from just one university**—rather than a diverse, randomly selected group—**limits how broadly the results can be applied**. The within-subjects design (measuring the same participants before and after) helps control for individual differences but doesn’t account for external factors that could influence stress levels.
